class_id: a retry budget charged for outcomes that could not have succeeded, so a configuration gap retires the work item as if it had genuinely failed
feature: any bounded-retry queue (attempts cap, backoff, dead-letter) whose failure outcomes mix 'we asked and it failed' with 'we could not ask at all because of how we are configured'
symptom: a work item is retried until an attempts ceiling stops it, and every attempt is counted the same way — but some failures are facts about CONFIGURATION (no adapter registered, no mapping for this field, no document type declared), not about the item. Those attempts cannot succeed until the configuration changes, so the budget burns in the first few cycles and the item is retired. When the configuration is later fixed, nothing reopens the retired items: the ceiling is a claim-time filter, and the event that would have made them askable (a manifest version bump, a new adapter) does not touch the counter. Generic test: for each outcome class, ask 'could re-asking with the same configuration ever change the answer?' — if not, it must not spend retry budget, and the configuration-change event must be wired to reopen what it retired. Corollary seen in the same data: a counter shared between an uncapped state (NOT_AVAILABLE_YET) and a capped one (CHECK_FAILED) lets the uncapped state pre-spend the capped state's budget, so a row's FIRST real failure can arrive already past the ceiling.
first_seen: 2026-09-23 -- IPODhan #884. recordOutcome charged attempts + 1 on every CHECK_FAILED, including COVERAGE_GAP ('<SOURCE> has no mapped field for …', 'no documentType in manifest for this field') and SOURCE_UNREACHABLE via NO_FETCHER_REGISTERED; the claim query stops at FIELD_PLAN_RECLAIM_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5. Measured read-only on ipodhan_staging: 6,624 CHECK_FAILED rows at attempts >= 5; the repair dry run resets 4,811 across 72 IPOs (CHITTORGARH no-mapping 3,250; BSE 898; DOC no-documentType 288; NSE 227; NSE no-fetcher 144; DOC column read 4) and holds 1,813 real ones (1,780 'no document provenance … (extractor gap or field absent)', 33 'no field result returned'). The above-cap rows (101 per IPO at attempts 6/8/9/13 on himalayan-solar, coreintegra-consulting, adroit-industries, bench-mark-infotech) came from the uncapped NOT_AVAILABLE_YET leg: each row was asked N times as NOT_AVAILABLE_YET (attempts + 1 each) and flipped to CHECK_FAILED once the document arrived, landing past the cap on its first real failure.
fix_prs: #884 fix: recordOutcome skips the increment when the recorded cause is a configuration gap (one list, packages/shared/src/utils/field-plan-config-gap.ts); the walk records a config-gap cause only when EVERY rank failed that way (classifyWalkFailures), so a real failure on any rank still counts; config-gap rows re-ask at claim priority 2 (after real re-asks); manifest reconciliation (updateRanksForVersion) resets attempts for config-gap CHECK_FAILED rows only; repair-config-gap-plan-attempts.ts resets the stranded rows (dry run default, --apply, --undo from the before-image ledger). Failing tests first on ipodhan_test (5 red, exit 1), green after. The NOT_AVAILABLE_YET-pre-spends-the-cap corollary is NOT fixed here: it needs a separate failure counter (a migration, owner-gated).
